primary_metric: net zero-day daily Sharpe of per-session pip P&L at 0.5 pip/side
result_summary: REJECT on both gates and both session definitions. Gross NEGATIVE on all 4 pairs: fxday median -0.548 pips/trade, active -0.455. 0/4 pairs reach Sharpe +0.30 (best -0.356). 88 of 96 declared cells have negative gross; best cell +0.241 pips vs 1.0 pip round-trip cost. kill_test: Inverted-entry explanation requires: (1) >=3 of 4 FX pairs with >=2 horizons at mean<0 and cluster-t<=-2; (2) NQ and ES positive on the same measurement; (3) fade beats momentum on gross. Tradable requires fade net pips/trade > 0 on >=3 of 4 pairs.
data_scope: as EXP-0001 plus NQ/ES 1m RTH from futures/nq/data/
primary_metric: per-signal mean signed forward return after a band break, session cluster-robust t
result_summary: INVERSION REJECTED (2/4 pairs, needed 3/4) and NOT TRADABLE (2/4). Futures reference PASSES on the identical code path (NQ +4.7..+24.5 ticks, cluster-t +2.4..+4.0; ES +1.0..+2.7) so the measurement is sound and the sign genuinely differs by asset class. FX carries ~10x less info per band-width (mean/bw -0.062..+0.061 vs NQ +0.030..+0.103) with no reliable sign; momentum direction SIGN-FLIPS between the two session definitions for EUR and GBP. Weak short-horizon reversion in AUD/NZD (-0.09..-0.19 pips, t -2.4..-4.4) is 5-11x smaller than the 1.0 pip round trip. MAJOR METHOD FINDING: per-signal and session-averaged estimands disagree in SIGN (GBPUSD fxday +0.010 vs -9.655 pips, t +0.01 vs -16.70) because signal count is endogenous to the outcome (corr +0.41); correcting to cluster-robust per-signal inference FLIPPED this run's verdict, and the same reversal appears on NQ/ES.
notes: Exit-neutral arm (stop_ref='none') isolates entry from exit geometry per rule 15. fade|stop=both cell is degenerate (stops out next bar) and excluded. Preregistered criterion 3 was badly specified (exact algebraic mirror in the exit-neutral cell) and is recorded as such rather than dropped.

kill_test: Anchor explanation REJECTED unless a structural anchor reaches |pooled_t|>=2.0, same sign on >=3 of 4 pairs, AND frac(placebo |t| >= structural |t|) <= 0.10 against the 24-hour placebo family. VALIDITY GATE: the NQ 09:30 positive control must satisfy the same three criteria or the run is INCONCLUSIVE.
data_scope: EURUSD/GBPUSD/AUDUSD/NZDUSD 1m 2011-07-19..2026-07-17 (NZD from 2011-12-06) + NQ 1m ETH 2011-07-31..2026-07-14; archived price-only FX files, SHA-256 verified vs futures_volume_manifest.json spot_input_sha256
primary_metric: per-signal mean signed 60-min forward return in band half-widths, pooled over pairs, matched fire rate, embargo=1 (open[t+2]), date-clustered t
result_summary: REJECT. Positive control PASSES at NQ native 390-min length (RTH_OPEN 09:30 mean/bw +0.0369, t +3.68, rank 2/19, frac 0.056; the only placebo above it is 09:15, the same boundary) and FAILS at the forced 1425-min length (same anchor t +1.60, frac 0.208) - so session LENGTH, not the anchor, drove the first failed control. All four structural FX anchors FAIL in both arms: best is NY_ROLL @1425 t -3.64 frac 0.125, and @390 t -2.54 frac 0.167. DECISIVE: 24/24 FX placebos are negative at 1425 and 23/24 at 390, i.e. mild reversion at EVERY hour = a property of the tape, not of any anchor. Best structural anchor stands 2.3-2.5x above its family median effect vs 21x for NQ. Sign is reversion throughout, so even at face value the momentum construct points the wrong way. Sensitivity (NOT adopted): filtering placebos to stability>=0.98 would pass NY_ROLL/TOK_OPEN at frac 0.045 - but only in the @1425 arm, whose own control fails; at 390 it still fails. No Null C (gate rule).
notes: HYP-0003 Amendment 1 (session length parameterised, NQ native-length control added) was written AFTER the first control failure and is labelled as such. Two defects found and fixed mid-run: resolution-dependent astype(int64) minute index collision, and an exploding cluster-t on degenerate cells whose NaN would have counted as a placebo pass (LEARNINGS 5). 17 invariants in tests/test_anchors.py gate the run.
